title: House prices were flat in July, Sydney and Melbourne are now slightly down for the year
excerpt: Home prices across Australia did not move in July. Sydney and Melbourne are now a little bit cheaper than a year ago, while Brisbane and Perth are still going up.
body:
Australian house prices did not move in July, according to the monthly home value index from CoreLogic, the company that tracks property prices across the country. Over the year to July, prices across Australia are up just 1.4 per cent, which is much slower than the 8 to 10 per cent growth we had in 2023 and 2024.

Sydney and Melbourne are now slightly cheaper than they were a year ago, down 0.4 per cent and 0.2 per cent. The growth is concentrated in the smaller capitals: Brisbane is up 5.1 per cent, Perth up 7.8 per cent, Adelaide up 4.3 per cent. People are still moving to these cities because they are cheaper than Sydney and Melbourne, and that demand is keeping prices up.

Rents across Australia went up 0.3 per cent in July, the smallest monthly increase since early 2022. Over the year, rents are up 4.8 per cent, which is now lower than the cost-of-living increase for the first time in four years.

Our take: this is the third month in a row that prices in Sydney and Melbourne have been flat or falling. The interest rate cuts from earlier in the year are no longer pushing prices up. If you are a first-home buyer in Brisbane or Perth, the window to buy before prices catch up to Sydney and Melbourne is closing. If you already own in Sydney or Melbourne, do not expect to make money on a quick sale, but you are also not at risk of a big drop. The market is in a steady state.
whatItMeans: If you are buying your first home in Sydney or Melbourne: The market is flat to soft. There is no rush. Negotiate hard on the price and on the settlement terms. Sellers are more willing to deal than they were a year ago.
If you are upgrading: The days when you could buy, do a quick reno, and sell for 10 per cent more are over. Plan to hold for at least five to seven years, not two to three.

If you are an investor: Rents are still growing but slowing down. The maths on negatively-geared investments (where the rental income does not cover the loan interest) has got harder. Look at the gross yield, the rent as a percentage of the property value, not just the headline price.

If you are a first-home buyer in Brisbane or Perth: The First Home Guarantee, which lets you buy with a smaller deposit, has not changed. If you can afford the loan repayments, now is as good a time as any.
